To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the H1 neuron responds to saccadic turns, and to the translation between saccades; (2) these responses can be separated by replaying modified stimuli; and (3) the responses of H1 can be explained by its function as a sccadic suppressor for figure-ground discrimination and as an increase in SNR for wide-field translation-sensitive neurons.

the blowfly H1 neuron, which responds to fast saccades and slow forward translation, has a dual function: it suppresses the activity of saccade-sensitive neurons and enhances the SNR of translation-sensitive neurons.
the H1 neuron responds with a transient burst to saccades and a tonic response between saccadic turns during naturalistic flight.

the function of neurons in the visual system of flying insects, and in particular the function of the H1 cell, a neuron in the optic lobe of the fly that is sensitive to the direction of movement of the animal in space.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the H1 neuron acts as a saccade suppressor for figure-ground discrimination during flight and, in addition, increases the SNR of translational flow detection during intersaccades.
the H1 neuron functions as a saccade detector for figure-ground discrimination, and a translational flow detector for object distance estimation.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a detailed analysis of naturalistic stimuli is essential to understand the function of a neuron in a complex natural environment.
a simple movement-sensitive neuron like H1 can have a complex function in naturalistic situations.
